description: Heavy-stutter / hard-block reconstruction test corpus. Each script simulates the verbatim ASR output (Whisper or device ASR) that a speaker with hard silent blocks would produce. Ground-truth 'intended' is what the speaker meant to say. Reconstruction quality is scored against intended, not against disfluent.
design_notes: Distinct from tests/stutter_pipeline/test_cases.json (which covers audible disfluencies). This corpus targets the silent-block / hard-block case George specifically needs to clear before foundation outreach. Patterns drawn from: SEP-28k block-labeled clips (Apple 2021), FluencyBank Timestamped (Bayerl 2024), Howell 2004 disfluency taxonomy, plus George's lived speech-block phenomenology.
v2_changes: Initial version used synthetic [BLOCK] markup that Whisper would never produce. v2 replaces those tokens with realistic Whisper behavior on silence: either dropped entirely (no text emitted during silence) or filled with documented Whisper hallucination phrases ('thank you for watching', 'thanks for watching', 'subscribe', 'thanks'). This makes the corpus faithful to what the engine actually sees in production.
block_token_convention: v2: no [BLOCK] tokens. Silent blocks manifest as either (a) absence of expected words in the disfluent input, or (b) Whisper hallucination strings inserted where silence was. '...' = audible pause / breath. '--' = mid-word abandonment. Lowercase, no end punctuation, mirrors raw Whisper output.

cases.type: hard silent block on /p/ onset, Whisper hallucinates
cases.intended: I want to present the proposal on Tuesday
cases.disfluent: i want to thank you for watching present the proposal on tuesday
cases.notes: Two silent freezes before the hard /p/ content word. Whisper fills the gap with its most common hallucination phrase ('thank you for watching' is the canonical Whisper-on-silence artifact). Lavrentiy must drop the hallucination and reassemble.

cases.type: Whisper hallucinated word during silent block
cases.disfluent: can you so so so call the doctor
cases.notes: Classic Whisper failure mode: silence triggers hallucination of high-frequency token ('so'). Lavrentiy must recognize 'so so so' as filler not intent.

cases.type: long silent block, Whisper hallucinates, then audible restart
cases.intended: My biggest concern is the deadline
cases.disfluent: my biggest thanks for watching uhh my my biggest concern is the deadline
cases.notes: Speaker abandons mid-phrase, freezes (Whisper hallucinates 'thanks for watching'), breathes, restarts the same phrase. False-start detection plus block recovery plus hallucination removal.

cases.intended: I think we should reschedule the meeting
cases.disfluent: i think we sh-- we should res-- we should reschedule the meeting
cases.notes: Two mid-word abandonments before the blocked word completes. Lavrentiy must drop the abandoned fragments without losing the eventual completion.

cases.disfluent: i agree with i mean i i disagree with the recommendation
cases.notes: Speaker says opposite-meaning placeholder to escape the block then corrects. Self-correction rule must respect 'I mean' as canonical-overwrite signal, not as discourse marker to drop.

cases.intended: The cost is forty thousand dollars
cases.disfluent: the cost is uh fourteen actually forty thousand dollars
cases.notes: Number-substitution self-correction. Reconstruction must take 'forty' over 'fourteen' and drop both the filler and the original wrong number.

cases.type: multiple silent blocks under phone stress, mixed with hallucination
cases.intended: Hi this is George I am calling about the appointment on Thursday
cases.disfluent: hi this is thanks for watching g g george i am calling about the the appointment on thursday
cases.notes: Three silent blocks. First triggers Whisper hallucination, others manifest as dropped content. Plus part-word repetition on the proper noun. Tests proper-noun preservation through a hallucinated gap.

cases.intended: I need to talk to my manager about the raise
cases.disfluent: i need to uhm uh well you know like uhm talk to my manager about the the raise
cases.notes: Heavy filler cluster used as a postponement strategy before the feared content word ('talk' triggers block). Different mechanism than h07's overt block but functionally equivalent.

cases.type: email dictation with silent blocks (dropped) plus repetitions
cases.intended: Please send the revised contract before close of business Friday
cases.disfluent: please uhh please please send the the revised contract uh before close of of business friday
cases.notes: Three repetition events. Silent block before content word manifests as dropped (no Whisper hallucination this time). Tests reconstruction across silent gaps without hallucination signal.

cases.type: block on proper noun, Whisper hallucinates
cases.intended: I met with Henderson at the Marriott yesterday
cases.disfluent: i met with thank you for watching henderson at the the m m marriott yesterday
cases.notes: Silent block on first proper noun, filled by Whisper with 'thank you for watching' hallucination. Part-word repetition on second proper noun. Tests proper-noun preservation under hallucination contamination.

cases.type: opening freeze in presentation, dropped content
cases.intended: Good morning everyone today I want to talk about the quarterly results
cases.disfluent: good uhm good morning everyone uh today i i want to talk about the the quarterly results
cases.notes: Opening freeze: speaker emits 'good', long silent freeze (Whisper drops, no hallucination this time), recovery, full restart. Common presentation-stress pattern.

cases.type: medical context with mid-word abandonment plus dropped silent block
cases.intended: I have been experiencing chest pain for about two weeks
cases.disfluent: i have been experiencing uhh ch-- ch-- chest pain for about uh two weeks
cases.notes: Two mid-word abandonments on the medically-loaded word. Silent block resolves into successful completion (no Whisper hallucination). Domain pack medical may engage at L3+.

cases.type: casual chat with sparse blocks, Whisper hallucinates 'thanks'
cases.disfluent: want to uh g g grab dinner thanks tonight
cases.notes: Friend-tone test. Whisper emits a stray 'thanks' during a brief silent block before the final word. Reconstruction must keep informal voice and drop the hallucination.

cases.type: legal context with block on stakes-laden phrase, Whisper hallucinates
cases.intended: I do not consent to that condition
cases.disfluent: i do not thank you for watching consent to that uh that condition
cases.notes: Block on the most consequential phrase, filled by Whisper hallucination. Reconstruction must drop the hallucination AND must NOT soften 'do not consent' to something hedged.

cases.type: bilingual EN-RU with Russian filler postponing English block, dropped
cases.intended: Can you please pass me the salt
cases.disfluent: can you ну ну please p p pass me the salt
cases.notes: Russian filler 'ну' used to postpone the English-onset block. Silent micro-block resolves into successful completion. George profile bilingual case.

cases.type: Whisper hallucinates 'the' during long silent block
cases.intended: I went to the conference last weekend
cases.disfluent: i went to the the the the conference last weekend
cases.notes: Whisper fills a 3-second silent block with repeated 'the' tokens. Lavrentiy must collapse, not preserve.

cases.intended: I think the new policy is unfair to junior staff
cases.disfluent: i think the new the the i i think the new policy is unfair to to junior staff
cases.notes: Speaker starts sentence, blocks, abandons, restarts identical sentence. Lavrentiy must recognize the abandonment-restart pattern and emit one clean sentence.

cases.type: block forces synonym substitution, Whisper drops the block
cases.intended: I need to call my therapist
cases.disfluent: i need to uh c c reach out to my therapist
cases.notes: Speaker blocks on 'call', substitutes 'reach out to'. Silent block during the abandonment manifests as dropped (no hallucination). If covert profile flags 'call' as avoided, ALWAYS RESTATE should restore 'call'. If not, preserve 'reach out to'. Tests covert-avoidance logic.
